source.quote: Ferrum's own page for the ERCO Gen 2 headphone DAC/amp, read 2026-11-27 with curl. Specifications: « DAC chip: ESS Sabre ES9028PRO »; « DAC resolution: PCM up to 768k @32bit; DSD up to 512 ( 22.6 MHz / 24.6 MHz ) »; « Digital inputs: USB-C (MQA, up to PCM 32-bit/ 768kHz, DSD512, DoP256 ); S/PDIF coaxial (MQA, up to PCM 24-bit/192 kHz, DoP64); S/PDIF optical (MQA, up to PCM 24-bit/96 kHz guaranteed, should work up to PCM 24-bit/192 kHz and DoP64 – depends of user’s optical cable and transmitter) ». On the filter: « SERCE’s DSP engine provides oversampling using DDF preferred HQ Apodizing digital filter ».

facts.chip: ESS ES9028PRO (« DAC chip: ESS Sabre ES9028PRO »), behind Ferrum's own SERCE DSP doing the oversampling and an in-house I/V stage.

_optical_96_guaranteed_and_the_rest_cond: « up to PCM 24-bit/96 kHz guaranteed, should work up to PCM 24-bit/192 kHz and DoP64 – depends of user’s optical cable and transmitter ». The same wording, and the same choice, as ferrum/wandla: 96000 is the guaranteed figure and the one recorded, and DoP64 on optical is left OUT for the same reason - the maker conditions it on the cable. Coaxial gets DoP64 unconditionally.
_usb_DSD512_native_by_subtraction: USB is rated « DSD512, DoP256 »: two DSD figures, one marked DoP. dsd_max DSD512 and dop_max DSD256 hold exactly that. native_dsd_possible is NOT written: the page never says « native », and DSD512 above a DoP256 ceiling implies a non-DoP path without naming it.
_the_oversampling_is_Ferrums_not_the_chi: « SERCE’s DSP engine provides oversampling using DDF preferred HQ Apodizing digital filter » - the oversampling filter runs in Ferrum's own DSP ahead of the ESS part. No bypass or NOS position is stated, so correctable is not written.
